newsitem.title: USA: Trump promises development in Detroit casino bid.
newsitem.headline: Trump promises development in Detroit casino bid.

text.p: Donald Trump said Thursday he would do for downtrodden Detroit what he has done for Atlantic City, N.J., and Gary, Ind. -- boost the local economy as well as build a "spectacular" casino.
Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. is among several casino developers seeking licenses to build three land-based casinos narrowly approved by Detroit voters in a referendum last year.
"I think we'll be doing development way beyond the casino ... should we be chosen," Trump said at a news conference prior to a luncheon designed to drum up civic support.
"We look forward to doing a great job for Detroit ... it will be spectacular," Trump said.

Trump's local partner in the casino bid, former Detroit Lion football star and black auto dealer Mel Farr, draped a red superman cape over Trump's shoulders, pronouncing him the best man for the job because of his "charisma and his track record" in Atlantic City and Gary.

"We're not just talking about gaming. We're talking about development in the inner city of Detroit," Farr said, adding that he had turned down competing partnership offers by other aspirants for casino licenses.
Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer plans to pare the applicants down to three by November, with licenses granted and ground-breaking scheduled for early next year.

MGM Grand Inc. announced its casino bid in February with local partners, and others expressing interest or proposing development bids were Mirage Resorts Inc., Harrah's Entertainment, Detroit businessman and casino boat owner Don Barden and a group of local businessmen including former Mayor Coleman Young.
Detroit would be the largest U.S. city with land-based casinos, although many cities are within fairly easy reach of either land- or water-based casinos.
Across the Canadian border in Windsor, Ontario, casinos have proven extremely profitable by pulling customers from the Detroit area, Trump noted.

Trump emphasised that his experience as a housing, condominium and office developer in New York City would be instrumental in Detroit, and he pledged $14 million to help clean up the city's huge stock of abandoned and dilapidated housing.
"There's no developer that's close to us in New York and no casino operator that's close to us in Atlantic City. Detroit wants housing and we are better qualified," he said.

His company's cash balance was approaching $200 million and was healthier than many other "struggling" casino operators, Trump said. His two Atlantic City casinos were the top two among the dozen operating there, he added.
Trump defended the benefits of casinos to the overall health of Atlantic City.

"Atlantic City 15 years ago was truly in terrible shape. Atlantic City today is truly a thriving community," he said, adding that he envisioned a more "family-oriented atmosphere" in a Detroit casino-hotel compared with the gaming-oriented New Jersey beachfront city.

Similarly, Trump said conditions in Gary, Ind., the nation's murder capital in the early 1990s, have improved since two floating casinos opened. The benefits have primarily stemmed from the thousands of jobs his casinos provide, he said.
